why: suitable must also require the open-floor-per-player ratio to clear MIN_OPEN_FLOOR_PER_PLAYER -- dropping roomOk from the conjunction leaves a board with plenty of separation and concealment but almost no floor space reading as suitable. Caught by 2 of the 12 cases in versus-board.test.ts: the 7x7 pillar-room fixture (39 open-floor cells, separation and concealment measuring true at every N while the ratio drops below the bound at N=3 and N=4) and the versusBoardCatalog test built against the same fixture at N=4. Equivalent to the concealment entry above in shape but not in effect -- this one changes a different conjunct and is caught by a different, deliberately non-overlapping fixture, so the two mutations cannot silently cover for each other. Count re-measured 2026-08-23: the pillar-room fixture's rescale to cellSize 2 (issue #225) consolidated the kill into 1 failing test. Count moved 1 -> 2 when the egress gate landed: the shipped sweep now asserts suitability per OFFERED combination as well, so dropping roomOk fails that assertion too.
killedBy: evaluateVersusBoard: room can fail, isolated from the other two measured: 39 open-floor cells; room passes at N=2 (19.5) and fails at N=3 (13) and N=4 (9.75), separation and concealment hold throughout
